title: Population movement
competency: Identify types and causes of population movement.

keywords.def: Moving from one part of a country to another part.
Moving across a country's border (the book's term for international migration).

ideas.name: Within a country and across borders

en.text: Population movement can be intra-national, within a country, or national, across a country's border. Intra-national migration can be rural to urban, urban to rural, rural to rural or urban to urban. Moving from Afar to Addis Ababa is intra-national; from Ethiopia to Saudi Arabia is across the border.

screens.title: Did she leave the country?
screens.ask: Tigist moves from a village in Afar to Addis Ababa. Did she cross a national border?
screens.after: No. Both places are in Ethiopia. This is movement within the nation: intra-national migration.

screens.title: 2.2.4 Population movement
paras: Population movement can be national (cross boundary) or intra-national (within a nation).
Intra-national migration is moving from one part of a country to another part.

screens.title: Examples
paras: People moving from the Afar region to Addis Ababa: intra-national migration.
People moving from Ethiopia to Saudi Arabia: national migration (across the border).

screens.title: Key words
defs: Moving from one part of a country to another part.
Moving across a country's border (the book's term for international migration).

screens.text: Moving from Ethiopia to Saudi Arabia is…

items: A farmer moves from a village near Jimma to Jimma town
A teacher moves from Hawassa city to a farm village
A trader moves from Adama to Dire Dawa
A family moves from one village to another village
screens.why: Name the starting place, then the arrival place.
screens.clue: Village = rural; town or city = urban.

screens.text: Can every movement be called migration, such as walking to the market each day?
opts: No, migration means moving to live in a new place
screens.ans: No, migration means moving to live in a new place
screens.why: Emigrants and immigrants move to live or make a new home. Daily trips are not migration.
screens.clue: Does the person change where they live?

screens.text: Abel moves from Bahir Dar to Nairobi for work. Which TWO labels fit?
screens.why: Bahir Dar and Nairobi are both cities, and Nairobi is in Kenya, so a border is crossed.
screens.clue: Are both places cities? Is Nairobi in Ethiopia?

items.text: 1. Can we consider all kinds of movement as migration?
opts: No, only moving to live in a new place
items.ans: No, only moving to live in a new place
items.why: Daily trips to work, school or market do not change where people live.
items.clue: Think of an emigrant or immigrant.

items.text: 2. Which are possible consequences of migration? Tap all.
pool: Loss of young workers in villages
a: Loss of young workers in villages
items.why: Migration affects both the place left and the place reached. Rain is not caused by migration.
items.clue: Think of the village and the city.

test.text: Moving within one country is called…
Moving from Afar to Addis Ababa is intra-national migration.
Moving from a village to a city is…
Which movement crosses a national border?
A doctor moves from Mekelle city to a rural village. This is…

notes.text: The book calls cross-border movement "national migration"; the standard term is "international migration". The lesson keeps the book's term and explains it as cross-border.
